clipboard: Let the agent read and write the clipboard (the get_clipboard and set_clipboard tools).
text_only: Never attach screenshots anywhere. The lowest token use, but the agent can't see pictures.
follow_new_windows: When an action opens a dialog or a menu, switch to it for the change report and the next look.
hot_reload: Apply changes to the settings file to running servers without a restart.
launch_timeout_secs: How long launch_app waits for a new app to show a window.
natural_mouse: Move the real mouse like a hand does: along a curve, speeding up and slowing down, with a faint tremor. Off: it jumps.
mouse_path: The way the real mouse goes. Mixed picks one at random for each move. Drags always go straight.
mouse_speed: How fast the real mouse moves, as a multiple of a hand's pace. 2 is twice as quick; some apps are slow to notice a very fast pointer.
mouse_overshoot: How often a long reach (over 250 px) goes a touch past its target and back, in percent of reaches. 0 never does. Only the hand style overshoots this way.
mouse_jitter: How much the path trembles, as a share of a hand's. 0 is a clean curve.
restore_pointer: Put your mouse pointer back where it was after the agent clicks, scrolls or drags, so it never takes your mouse away.
overlay.cursor_style: The agent's pointer. Random gives each session one, and a different one to each agent at once.
overlay.cursor_color: The colour of the plain arrow and the base of the pointer's ring.
overlay.cursor_tag: The name beside the pointer. Empty: no name.
overlay.cursor_motion: The pointer leans as it moves, leaves a trail, breathes, and shows drags and scrolls.
overlay.trail: The trail the pointer leaves as it moves, made of its own material (sparkles, flecks, frost, chrome drops). Needs cursor motion.
overlay.trail_strength: How long the trail is. 100 is as it was made; 0 leaves none.
overlay.lean_strength: How far the pointer leans into a move. 0 keeps it upright.
overlay.breathe: The pointer breathes while it waits: the jelly swells, the paper sways. Needs cursor motion.
overlay.cursor_path: How the pointer glides to where it acts.
overlay.show_keys: Show pressed keys as keycaps by the pointer, and typed text running out beside it.
overlay.click_effect: A ripple where the agent clicks.
overlay.show_cursor: Draw the agent's own pointer. The real mouse is never moved for this.
overlay.move_ms: How long the pointer takes to glide. An action waits for it to arrive.
overlay.scale: Size multiplier for everything the overlay draws. 0 follows the display scaling.
overlay.enabled: Show the on-screen indicator while the agent works. It is click-through and left out of the agent's screenshots.
overlay.show_border: A glowing border around the screen or window the agent works on.
overlay.border_target: Whether the border goes around the whole screen or only the window worked on.
overlay.border_width: The bright core line of the border.
overlay.glow_size: How far the glow fades out. 0 is a plain line.
overlay.label_working: Label while the agent acts on the computer.
overlay.label_thinking: Label while the model is thinking.
overlay.label_done: Label when the work is finished.
overlay.label_paused: Label while it waits for you to stop using the mouse and keyboard.
overlay.label_stopped: Label after the emergency stop. {hotkey} becomes the stop key.
overlay.color_thinking: Colour while the model is thinking.
overlay.color_done: Colour when the work is finished.
overlay.done_after_ms: No new action for this long: the work counts as done.
overlay.done_linger_ms: How long "done" stays before everything disappears.
overlay.transition_ms: Blend from one state colour to the next over this time.
overlay.capture_hide_ms: X11 only: the pause after hiding the overlay before a screenshot.
overlay.font: A font file for the label. Empty: a system font.
overlay.command: A helper program for the overlay, for programs that embed the library.
screenshot.attach: When a look includes a picture: auto (first view, a big change, or a sparse tree), always (most tokens) or never.
screenshot.auto_sparse_threshold: In auto mode, attach a picture when the tree has fewer interactive elements than this.
screenshot.max_dimension: The longest edge of a picture. This is the main image-token setting: 1024 costs about 35% less than 1280.
screenshot.overview_max_dimension: A smaller size for pictures of windows whose tree already says what is there. 0: always the size above.
screenshot.png_compression: PNG compression. It changes the file size only.
screenshot.scope: Follow-up pictures of a screen the model has seen: only the part that changed (auto), or the whole window (full).
screenshot.region_max_ratio: A change bigger than this share of the window sends the whole window.
screenshot.region_min_size: The changed part is at least this big on each side, for context.
screenshot.adaptive: Leave pictures out of well-described windows once the model has looked a few times without using pixels there.
screenshot.smart: Leave out a picture when all that changed is what the tree already reports.
screenshot.record_apps: Count how often each app needed pixels (the doctor command shows it).
screenshot.locate_picture: Locate sends the window with the places it found numbered.
screenshot.icon_sprite: Experimental: when no picture is attached, a small strip of the buttons that have no name, numbered.
tree.max_walk: Elements read from the app before pruning.
tree.max_text_len: Characters of text or value shown per element.
tree.show_actions: Show the actions each element offers.
tree.show_states: Show states such as focused, disabled and checked.
tree.diff: Later looks return only what changed.
tree.diff_full_ratio: Show the whole tree when more than this share changed.
tree.report_changes: Add the state after the action to an action's result.
tree.report_changes_max_lines: At most this many lines of changes in a report.
tree.report: What a report says: full (every change), relevant (around what was acted on) or brief (counts).
tree.max_tokens: Token budget of one tree. Bigger trees are shortened. 0: no limit.
tree.summarize: How a tree over the budget is shortened: normal (fold, then cut), light (only fold lists) or off.
tree.fold_keep: Items kept at the start of a folded list (and 2 at its end).
tree.brief_repeats: Explain notes in full once, then briefly.
tree.compact: Say each thing once without losing anything: look-alike siblings as records, ranges of indices, and so on.
tree.quiet_volatile: Things that change on their own (clocks, spinners) are summed up in one line after a few reports.
tools.disabled: Tools the model never sees, for example drag or batch.
tools.enabled: If not empty, only these tools are offered.
tools.descriptions: How long the tool descriptions are. Lean uses the fewest tokens.
tools.manager: Which tools the model sees at first. Dispatch: the base tools plus find_tools, the rest on demand, and the list never changes.
tools.preset: Full: every tool the other settings allow. Small: a fixed small set for smaller models.
tools.default_app: A call without an app acts on the app of the last call that named one.
tools.launch_look: launch_app answers with the app's first state.
tools.design_steps: When design lists the steps to paint a design.
timing.settle_ms: Pause after each action before looking again.
timing.settle: Adaptive waits until the screen stops changing; fixed only pauses.
timing.settle_max_ms: The longest an adaptive wait lasts.
timing.settle_poll_ms: How often the screen is checked while waiting.
timing.key_delay_ms: Pause between keys in a key sequence.
timing.app_cache_ms: Reuse the running-app list for this long.
timing.wait_poll_ms: The default poll interval of wait_for.
timing.expect_wait_ms: How long an action with expect waits for the result to show.
timing.adaptive_grace: Say "nothing changed" after 200 ms instead of 500 for apps that show changes at once.
cache.enabled: Remember screens the model has seen: coming back to one sends only what differs.
cache.max_memory_kb: Memory the remembered screens may use.
cache.match_threshold: Share of common elements that counts as the same screen.
cache.dedupe_screenshots: Never send an unchanged picture of a screen twice.
cache.pixel_grid: Cells across the longer side for the picture fingerprint.
cache.pixel_tolerance: Brightness drift per cell still counted as unchanged.
cache.snapshot_ttl_ms: Reuse a read this recent if nothing ran since. 0: off.
cache.rebase_after_tokens: After this many tokens of results, send a tree whole again with a picture. 0: never.
ocr.mode: Read text off the screen for apps whose tree says little: auto (sparse trees only), always or off.
ocr.engine: The reader: the system's own, or Tesseract.
ocr.sparse_threshold: In auto mode, read when the tree has fewer interactive elements than this.
ocr.languages: Languages to read, for example en or de. Empty: your own languages.
ocr.min_confidence: Leave out lines recognised with less confidence.
ocr.blind_regions: Also read areas the tree says nothing about (a canvas, a picture) in windows that have plenty of other elements.
decision.auto: The server asks the model on its own where that saves the agent a turn.
decision.auto_timeout_ms: The longest wait for those questions.
decision.timeout_ms: The longest wait for one answer.
decision.max_state_chars: A longer state keeps its start and its end.
decision.parallel: Requests at once when judging several items.
decision.cache_seconds: The same question about the same state is answered once for this long.
privacy.redact_passwords: Mask password fields in text and black them out of pictures.
privacy.redact_card_numbers: Mask card numbers (only the last 4 digits stay).
privacy.redact_labels: Fields whose label contains one of these are masked too.
privacy.style: How private areas are hidden in pictures.
control.stop_hotkey: The emergency stop: stops the agent at once from any app. Empty: no stop key.
control.pause_on_user_input: Wait while you use the mouse or keyboard. Only the system idle time is read, never what you type.
control.resume_after_idle_ms: How long you must be idle before the agent continues.
control.max_pause_secs: After this long the action fails and the agent is told why.
control.settings_hotkey: Opens this panel from any app. Empty: no key.
hub.enabled: Several agents on one desktop share one hub: a cursor each, one stop key, the screen shared out, turns at the keyboard and mouse.
hub.port: The hub's port on this computer.
hub.arrange: With two agents or more, move each agent's window into its part of the screen.
hub.chat: Let the agents send each other short messages.
hub.turn_wait_secs: The longest an agent waits for its turn at the keyboard and mouse.
hub.release_after_secs: An agent that makes no call for this long gives its part of the screen to the others until its next call; a server that was only started has none.
notifications.enabled: Let the agent read desktop notifications. They carry other apps' messages and codes.
notifications.apps: Only notifications from these apps. Empty: any app.
script.saved_as_tools: Each saved script is also a tool of its own.
script.files: Files scripts may use: none, workspace (only the scripts folder's files), read (read any file) or all.
script.web: Let scripts fetch and download over http(s).
script.max_seconds: The longest run of one script, tool calls included.
script.dir: Where saved scripts are kept. Empty: the default folder.
verify.enabled: Check each action's result and tell the agent when it didn't work.
verify.retry: An action that clearly failed is tried once more another way.
verify.retry_on_no_change: Also retry presses after which nothing visible changed. Off: some actions (pay, send) show their effect late and must not be repeated.
audit.enabled: Write a line of metadata per call to a log file.
audit.path: The log file. Empty: audit.log in the server's folder.
server.instructions: The instructions sent when a client connects: full, short (for clients that load the skills) or off.
server.result_meta: For hosts that trim their context: results say which earlier results they repeat.
server.structured_output: Also return some results as data, for clients that use it.
server.http_addr: Serve MCP over HTTP at this address, for example 127.0.0.1:8787. Empty: stdio only.
server.http_token: The bearer token HTTP clients must send.
update.enabled: Look for updates and download them. Off: it never updates by itself.
update.check_after_mins: Minutes after the server starts before the first look.
update.check_every_hours: Hours between looks while the server runs. Used when the minutes below are 0.
update.check_every_mins: Minutes between looks, for a shorter wait than an hour. At least 5. 0: use the hours.
update.channel: Stable takes only proper releases. Prerelease also takes releases GitHub marks as pre-releases (their tags are plain numbers, such as v4.9.0).
update.pin: A version to stay on, for example 5.0.2: only that release is taken, and nothing newer. Empty: the newest.
update.skip_version: A version never to take, for example one that went wrong here.
update.install: When a downloaded update goes in: restart (after the computer restarts), start (the next server start) or manual.
update.repo: The GitHub repository releases come from (owner/name).
linux.batch_size: Elements whose AT-SPI queries run at once.
linux.text_max_chars: The longest text read from a text element.
macos.batch_attributes: Read all of an element's attributes in one call.
windows.use_cache_request: Fetch a whole window's tree in one UIA call.
panel.theme: Light, dark, or follow the computer.
panel.accent: The colour the panel's palette is made from.
panel.language: The language of this page: the browser's, English, Persian (right to left), Chinese or Russian.
panel.port: The port the panel listens on while it is open. A free one is used if this one is taken.
panel.idle_minutes: The panel closes after this long without a request.
